clue.text: Gentle type

definitions.meaning: gentle means tender and considerate towards others
a type is a sort, class or variety

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a benevolent, tender person, and a category or sort of thing.

clue.text: Fibre for making red hat

indicators.note: the letters of the two following words are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chooses yarn with which to knit a red hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the signal: the six letters of RED HAT are reshuffled into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand of spun fibre used in sewing or weaving is the synonym needed.

clue.text: A long step on a horse

parts.note: a stride is a long step in walking or running

explanation.surface: A rider takes a long step up onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits with one leg on each side of the mount, the classic posture for riding.

clue.text: Businessman who holds a handle

parts.note: a dealer in candles or ship's supplies, read playfully as a word that carries the word handle inside its letters

explanation.surface: A merchant grips a handle as he works.
explanation.walkthrough: The trader's name literally contains HANDLE, framed by C and R; the clue gives no separate words for those two letters, so it reads as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in supplies, as in a ship's provisioner, is a trader or businessman.

clue.text: Not oil mixed for a cosmetic preparation

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beauty product is mixed without any oil in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' makes an anagram of NOT OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin cream or liquid applied to the body is a typical cosmetic preparation.

clue.text: Nevertheless, people come here for enlightenment!

definitions.text: Nevertheless, people come here for enlightenment!

parts.words: Nevertheless, people come here for enlightenment!
parts.note: a place of evening classes, named after the dark hours, yet adults attend it to be educated

explanation.surface: Despite everything, seekers flock to this place in search of wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is darkness versus light: the place is named for the dark hours, yet people come there to be enlightened, that is, to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening classes for adults are where people go to learn after work, which is their enlightenment.

clue.text: Subversive group doesn't suggest foursquare support!

definitions.text: Subversive group doesn't suggest foursquare support!

parts.words: Subversive group doesn't suggest foursquare support!
parts.note: a body of traitors working from within, described as one pillar more than the four that hold up a square structure

explanation.surface: A group of rebels is hardly a picture of solid, four-pillared loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Foursquare means solid and loyal, and four columns support a square building; an extra pillar beyond the four is the treacherous one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the Spanish Civil War names secret sympathisers who undermine a side from within.

clue.text: Fire extinguisher for the horseman?

parts.note: a hand pump for dousing fires, braced with the foot in a loop, imagined as the rider's own piece of kit because of its foot loop

explanation.surface: A rider asks what equipment he should carry to fight fires.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime hand pump was held steady by a foot in a metal loop like the one a rider puts a foot in, hence the horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A small portable pump used against fires in Britain during the Second World War.

clue.text: It's a puzzle to make holes in

definitions.meaning: a conundrum or enigma posed as a question
to pierce something all over, as with bullets

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a conundrum and to perforate thoroughly, as in shot full of holes.

clue.text: Flee the coop!

definitions.meaning: to flee is to escape quickly on foot
a chicken coop is an enclosure for hens, also called by the word for a fenced pen

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to escape at speed and also an enclosed area where poultry are kept.

clue.text: A jot of Greece

parts.note: a tiny amount, which is also a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks for just a little bit of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a tiny amount is also the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is the Greek jot.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter came to mean the tiniest amount, exactly as jot does.

clue.text: Was at a meeting with a retinue

definitions.meaning: to be present at an event

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both was present at an event and accompanied by attendants or escorts.

clue.text: Look at the organ to do it

definitions.meaning: to look at something carefully, to watch it
the body part used for looking, the organ of sight

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to regard closely, and as a noun it is the organ of sight.

clue.text: They take passengers, in the main

definitions.text: They take passengers, in the main

parts.words: They take passengers, in the main
parts.note: large ships that carry passengers across the ocean, the main being the open sea

explanation.surface: Most of the time, these vehicles carry passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the sea, where these big passenger ships sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean-going passenger ships carry travellers across the high seas.

clue.text: Cries out there's a Devon delicacy in the ship

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as the delicacy is placed in the ship

parts.note: clotted cream is a famous Devon delicacy

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks on finding Devon treats on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Clotted cream is a thick cream from Devon in south-west England, eaten with scones.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out loudly is to shriek, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Fabulous girls got their reputation from sailors

definitions.text: Fabulous girls got their reputation from sailors

parts.words: Fabulous girls got their reputation from sailors
parts.note: mythical sea women, half fish, whose legend was spread by seamen's tales

explanation.surface: Glamorous young women owe their fame to the gossip of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like 'wonderful', but it means belonging to fable: these are legendary sea creatures known from seamen's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary sea creatures with a woman's body and a fish's tail, reported by sailors.

clue.text: Hard to have a dour arrangement with America

indicators.note: an arrangement is a new ordering, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: It is tough to come to a grim agreement with the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like a deal, but it signals an anagram: A DOUR becomes ARDUO, then US follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard in the sense of demanding great effort is strenuous and laborious.

clue.text: Run round the vessel

indicators.note: round suggests turning the letters about, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone jogs a lap around a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges the letters of RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase or container, often for ashes or tea, is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Good man, as likely as not, but he didn't live well!

definitions.text: Good man, as likely as not, but he didn't live well!

parts.words: Good man, as likely as not, but he didn't live well!
parts.note: a citizen of an ancient Greek city famed for discipline and courage, whose life was famously austere

explanation.surface: A decent fellow, probably, yet his way of life was far from comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't live well' means did without luxuries, not behaved badly: the ancient Greeks of this city were known for harsh, frugal living.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of the ancient Greek city of Sparta were famed for hardiness and austere, frugal lives.

clue.text: It's powerless to fly in the air

definitions.text: It's powerless to fly in the air

parts.words: It's powerless to fly in the air
parts.note: an aircraft without an engine that still flies, riding air currents

explanation.surface: Something is helpless and unable to get airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless to fly' reads as 'unable to fly', but it means flying without power, that is, with no engine.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft stays aloft on air currents, flying without power.

clue.text: But the housewife doesn't use it to spread a film

definitions.text: But the housewife doesn't use it to spread a film

parts.words: But the housewife doesn't use it to spread a film
parts.note: the cloth for cleaning, which removes powder, whereas its verb can also mean sprinkling a fine film of powder

explanation.surface: A homemaker will not use a certain cloth for spreading a thin layer.
explanation.walkthrough: To dust can mean to remove dust or to sprinkle a fine layer, as of sugar on a cake; the cleaning cloth only does the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used for wiping dust off furniture is a household cleaning item.

clue.text: Level bargains at the greengrocer's?

parts.note: par means level or equal, as in on a par
a snip is a bargain in British slang

explanation.surface: A shopper finds that prices are evenly cheap at the vegetable shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain; the whole clue then points to root vegetables sold by a greengrocer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale root vegetables sold by greengrocers, so the clue's shop scene points to them.

clue.text: Get a different sort as cooks

indicators.note: different means made otherwise, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone receives another type, as chefs do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' signals the anagram of SORT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook in an oven with dry heat is the verb needed, matching cooks.

clue.text: I leave an African tribe, the devils!

indicators.note: leave means go away, so the letter named is taken out of the following word

parts.note: impis are bands of Zulu warriors, a South African fighting regiment

explanation.surface: Someone departs from an African people, calling them devils.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors; take one I out of IMPIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Little devils or mischievous sprites are the small demons of folklore.

clue.text: Tune in Fairyland

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the clue word that follows

explanation.surface: Music plays in a magical land of fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside FAIRYLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody, as in a song's tune, is a classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Take for granted it's to adopt

definitions.meaning: to suppose something is true without proof
to take on a manner, role or appearance

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to suppose without proof and to take on a role or manner.

clue.text: Certain about the employer

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters of the synonym are rearranged

parts.note: a user employs something, so the one who employs is a user

explanation.surface: Someone is confident about their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges USER, a synonym for the employer, one who employs something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being certain means being confident and positive, without doubt.

clue.text: They're studied, so to speak, in schools

definitions.text: They're studied, so to speak, in schools

parts.words: They're studied, so to speak, in schools
parts.note: principals of schools, who are, in a manner of speaking, closely watched by their pupils

explanation.surface: Certain subjects are examined, as it were, in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studied' seems to mean learned like a subject, but the people in charge of schools are 'studied' in the sense of being watched by the pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Male principals in charge of schools, the heads of the teaching staff.
